analysis:
The supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (base lines 664-1123), so nothing in them is a head-side code change. The file_changes patch shows the head diff only as documentation: the stale v0.9.21 candidate heading is replaced, and a v0.10.0 candidate section and historical-version notes are added. No executable code, config, wire protocol or auth logic is modified in the supplied evidence, so no concrete regression or new attack surface can be shown.

The base text records prior security-relevant decisions. T-041/SEC-035 covers the 30-minute SSD prefix-cache TTL, with the epoch-retention change explained as not weakening the KEK-wipe purge or AES-GCM authentication. Other entries cover App Attest rotation limits, fail-closed authorization fences, and graceful drain. These match the T-041 definition (30 min, env can only shorten, epoch not a purge primitive), and I saw no contradiction.

The patch excerpt is truncated. It describes a v0.10.0 candidate with a request-normalization v8 to v9 bump, MLX and mlx-swift dependency pin changes, and new model onboarding. The mismatch handling it describes is that a coordinator attaches a cache scope only when contract IDs match. That fails cold rather than sharing across scopes, which is consistent with the T-041 isolation posture. The actual implementations (cache salt derivation, prompt-contract checks, Metal kernel changes, provider-version floors) are outside the supplied evidence. Those claims are changelog prose only, not verified controls. The next pass should review the real source diffs for SSDPrefixCachePolicy TTL bounds, cacheSalt derivation, and the dependency-pin changes. Remaining uncertainty is low for this file alone.
